questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Thornbury Pharmaceuticals, a startup firm plans to sell a product in Yewton at $26 per unit. Variable cost is $16 per unit and fixed costs are $162,354. How many units must it sell to break even?
questions.explanation: Break-even volume equals fixed cost divided by contribution per unit, where contribution is price minus variable cost. Contribution here is $10, and $162,354 divided by that is about 16,236 units. Dividing by price alone or by variable cost alone ignores the true contribution, and adding variable cost to price overstates it. At the break-even point profit is zero.
questions.hint: Divide fixed cost by price minus variable cost.

options.misconception: ignores variable cost in the contribution margin
divides fixed cost by variable cost instead of contribution
adds variable cost to price instead of subtracting

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Linden Jewelry, a publicly-traded firm buys an item for $73 and sells it in Valeview for $106. What is the gross margin as a percentage of the selling price?
questions.explanation: Gross margin is gross profit divided by selling price. Gross profit is $33, and dividing by the $106 selling price gives 31 percent. The figure of 45 percent is the markup on cost, which uses cost as the denominator and is always larger. Mixing up margin and markup is a common pricing error that can badly understate the needed price.
questions.hint: Divide profit by the selling price, not by the cost.

options.misconception: computes markup on cost instead of margin on selling price
divides cost by gross profit instead of relating profit to selling price
reports cost as a share of price, the complement of margin

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Demand for a life-saving medicine sold by Jasper Foods, a mid-sized firm in Mapleridge changes very little when the price rises. Which statement about elasticity is most accurate?
questions.explanation: When quantity barely responds to price, demand is inelastic, with an absolute elasticity below 1. In that case the percentage gain in price outweighs the percentage loss in units, so total revenue rises. Necessities are a classic inelastic example because buyers have few alternatives.
questions.hint: Small quantity response means inelastic demand and a revenue gain from higher price.

options.text: Demand is unit elastic, so revenue is unchanged
options.misconception: assumes equal percentage changes without evidence
incorrectly excludes necessities from elasticity analysis

options.text: Demand is elastic, so a price rise lowers revenue
options.misconception: mistakes weak responsiveness for strong responsiveness

options.text: Demand is inelastic, so a price rise is likely to increase total revenue

questions.subject: MARKETING
questions.stem: Veldt Jewelry, a established firm sets the price of a new Zandale service by estimating what customers believe it is worth, then working backward to the costs it can afford to incur. Which pricing approach is this?
questions.explanation: Value-based pricing starts with the customer's perceived worth and works backward to costs, so the price captures the value delivered. Cost-plus pricing instead adds a markup to costs, and competition-based pricing anchors on rivals' prices. Penetration pricing is a low initial price to win share, which is a different decision.
questions.hint: Ask what the price is anchored to: customer worth or company cost.

options.misconception: mistakes customer worth for rivals' prices
confuses a value estimate with a low launch price
assumes price is set by adding a margin to cost
